# Studio Grata

> Interior architecture for spaces that host well. Studio Grata is an interior architecture studio in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, designing restaurants, bars, hotels, resorts, wellness spaces and workplaces across India.

We design every space around four numbers: capacity (how many it can host at peak), value (what each visit is worth), flow (how fast it resets or turns) and upkeep (how it ages). The studio is led by two design principals, Shirin KC and Amritha Madhavan, and one operating principal, Shifaz Salim.

Services: space planning, concept, interior architecture, furniture and styling, and site delivery.

Contact: reach@studiograta.in, +91 78998 29886. Enquiries: https://studiograta.in/connect

## Journal

- [The office has to earn the commute](https://studiograta.in/journal/earn-the-commute): Most Indian teams now have set office days. What the workplace research says people come in for, and how to design a startup or boutique office for its busiest day.
- [Fit out for the team you'll be in 18 months](https://studiograta.in/journal/fit-out-for-growth): A growing team can outgrow its office before the fit-out pays for itself. What a Bengaluru fit-out costs, when flex space makes sense, and what to design so it moves with you.
- [Renovate without closing](https://studiograta.in/journal/renovate-without-closing): Every week a hotel, restaurant or spa is closed is revenue that doesn't come back. How to plan a renovation in phases so the space keeps earning while the work happens.
- [Keep, refresh or replace](https://studiograta.in/journal/keep-refresh-replace): Most hotels, restaurants and spas don't need a new fit-out. They need the right things changed. How to decide what stays, what gets refreshed and what has to go.
- [Local is a supply chain, not a mood](https://studiograta.in/journal/local-materials): Regional materials can give a resort its sense of place. They can also delay its opening. How to source handmade and local materials for hotel volumes and deadlines.
- [Attic stock: the line item nobody budgets](https://studiograta.in/journal/attic-stock): Why one of the cheapest protections in a hotel fit-out is a locked storeroom of your own materials: what attic stock is, what to keep, how much, and where it goes wrong.
- [The view is on the rate card](https://studiograta.in/journal/view-on-the-rate-card): Guests pay for the setting. How reading the site before drawing decides which rooms earn the view, how spaces work through the day and year, and which materials last.
- [The trial class is a site visit](https://studiograta.in/journal/trial-to-member): First-timers decide whether to join long before the sales conversation. What the retention research says, and the six moments in a trial visit that your space controls.
- [How a room changes what people do](https://studiograta.in/journal/psychology-of-space): Where guests sit, how long they stay and what they spend are shaped by the room. What the research says, and how we design with it.
- [The Four Numbers: what your room earns per seat, per hour](https://studiograta.in/journal/four-numbers): What a restaurant or bar earns per seat, per hour, and the four numbers we design every space around: capacity, value, flow and upkeep.
